summary: Iter10: Phase 1 intake + AI interview end-to-end tested. Backend: 19/19 pytest passed (intake GET/PUT incl. persistence, interview start/reply/finish/active, authz: anon=401, student=403, non-owning parent=403/404, AI draft-mission for chore prompt contains no 'write it down' phrases, regression smoke for citations/skills/strategies/moments/games/public stats). Frontend: parent-open-intake link on Parent Dashboard navigates to /parent/students/<id>/intake with H1 'Tell us about Enzo', completion bar, 6 step jumpers (basics/adhd/interests/sensitivities/peak/vanderbilt), Basics select-save flow, chip add via Enter (lowercased) and suggestion-click, Vanderbilt step renders 76 buttons (~18 items x 4 Likert + headers), Save shows 'Profile saved.' toast. Interview modal: opener auto-renders, parent reply triggers AI response (no raw <<<WRAP_UP>>> token leaked), close-without-save works. Mission Detail clue captures correctly gated: shown for Reading: text evidence mission, NOT shown for EF: planning mission.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~2170 lines — increasingly hard to navigate. Strongly recommend splitting into routers (auth, students/intake, interviews, missions, research, public) before adding Phase 2.

StudentIntake.jsx is 644 lines and bundles InterviewModal inline. The modal is a self-contained feature (separate state, network calls, scroll ref) and should live in its own component file for testability and reuse.

Interview WRAP_UP detection uses substring `<<<WRAP_UP>>>` on the assistant reply, then sets sess['status']='completed' inside reply endpoint but does NOT synthesize the profile automatically — caller must still POST /finish. Worth either calling _finish internally on wrap-up or surfacing the wrap-up state to the UI more explicitly (currently only the save button visibility/copy hints at it).

POST /interviews/{sid}/reply returns 502 if the LLM call fails, but the parent reply was already appended to in-memory `sess.messages` — and then the function raises before persisting to Mongo. So a single transient LLM error silently drops the parent's message. Consider persisting the parent turn before the LLM call.
_ai_chat_with_history collapses history into a single user message instead of using true multi-turn conversation API — works but loses some quality vs sending role-tagged messages. Low priority.
interview_reply trims content to 2000 chars without surfacing a 400 to the client when input exceeds that — silent truncation. Either reject >2000 with 413 or document the limit in UI.

/api/students/{id}/intake returns an empty StudentProfile (all defaults) for a freshly-linked student rather than 404 — fine UX-wise, but document this since some consumers may want to distinguish 'never filled' from 'all cleared'.

PUT /api/students/{id}/intake uses profile.model_dump(exclude_none=False) which lets clients erase fields by sending nulls (intended), but there's no validation of vanderbilt list length (could submit a 1-item list).
